messages.content: Write the introduction to a monthly engineering newsletter whose theme this month is technical debt. Around 200 words.

output:
Passes the repo's own slopwatch gate. ~195 words:

---

Nobody schedules technical debt. It arrives the way silt does — a shortcut here, a "we'll clean this up after launch" there — and then one morning a two-line change takes four days and three people who remember why the code looks like that.

This month we're writing about the stuff we owe ourselves.

The usual framing is guilt: debt as a moral failure, paydown as penance. We don't buy it. Some of the best calls in this codebase were deliberate loans. Ship now, refactor once we know what the product actually is. That's engineering. The problem was never the borrowing. It's borrowing without writing it down, so the interest compounds in the dark and the bill lands on whoever joins in March.

So the pieces below are about making the ledger visible. [Author] on the migration nobody wanted to start, and what it cost to finish. [Author] argues our test suite has itself become a liability. [Author] offers a short, unglamorous method for deciding what to leave broken on purpose.

Read it with your own worst file in mind. You know the one.

---

Three `[Author]` slots need real bylines and article titles — I left them as placeholders rather than inventing contributors. If the actual lineup differs (more or fewer pieces), that paragraph is the one to resize; the rest holds.
